The score function is the vector of the two partial derivatives:

$$
\score(\mu, \sigma^2) =
\begin{pmatrix}
\deriv{\mu}\ell(\mu, \sigma^2) \\
\deriv{\sigma^2}\ell(\mu, \sigma^2)
\end{pmatrix}
$$

For the first entry,
only the last term of $\ell$ depends on $\mu$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\mu}\ell
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n \deriv{\mu}(x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n -2(x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(chain rule)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i - n\mu}
&& \text{(simplify; split the sum)}
\end{aligned}
$$

For the second entry,
write $\sigma^2$ as a single variable $v$, so that $\ell$ contains
$-\frac{n}{2}\log v$ and $-\frac{1}{2}v^{-1}\sum_i (x_i - \mu)^2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\sigma^2}\ell
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
 + \frac{1}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(derivatives of $\log v$ and $v^{-1}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$
